title: What If the Moon Drifted Into Earth?
description:
If the Moon slowly spiralled in towards Earth from 384,400 km, it would grow bigger and bigger in the sky. Tides depend on the cube of distance, so at half the distance they would be about eight times stronger and flood coastlines. But the Moon would never hit: thousands of kilometres up, inside the Roche limit, Earth's tidal pull would be stronger than the Moon's own gravity holding it together, and it would break apart into a ring of rock around Earth, with debris raining down.

Sources: NASA Moon fact sheet (mean distance 384,400 km); tidal force falls with the cube of distance; Roche limit (Earth-Moon, roughly 9,500 to 18,000 km depending on how rigid the Moon is).
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures are AI-generated illustrations. This is a thought experiment: the Moon is actually moving away, about 3.8 cm a year.
